summary: This Advent sermon explores biblical peace (shalom) as fullness and life as God intended, arguing that true peace comes only through submitting to Jesus as Prince of Peace. The pastor challenges Christians to stop letting political ideologies, screens, and cultural narratives rule their lives and instead rest in Christ, pursue enemy love, and become peacemakers in divided communities.
key_points: Biblical shalom means fullness and completeness, not merely absence of conflict
The quality and duration of peace depends on who or what rules your life
Christians must turn from screens and political tribes to rest in God's unconditional love
The church grows through sacrificial enemy love, not winning cultural wars
Believers should pray for peace for all people, even enemies, in global conflicts
big_idea: True and lasting peace comes only when we submit every area of our lives to the rule and reign of Jesus, the Prince of Peace, rather than letting political ideologies, cultural narratives, or other influences govern us.
title: ADVENT: Peace
